title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Garden maintenance and clean-ups
audience: Garden maintenance and clean-up operators, including solo operators, who sell one-off clean-ups and recurring garden plans at a price that reflects the result.
learningOutcomes: Write a garden clean-up offer with a clear promised result, a time frame, conditions and a return-visit guarantee
Identify the friction and risk a garden client carries and reduce them
Price a garden offer on value and on cost, and check it against the sourced market ranges

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will tidy your garden' is a service. 'I will clear the beds and paths, remove the cuttings and leaf litter, and send before and after photos within one working day. If I miss a bed, I will return free within a set window' is an offer. The client buys a tidy garden on a known date, with proof. The window and the timing are example wording; set them from your own job records. Where the waste goes must follow the rules that apply to your council and your state, which are not confirmed in this lesson.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome (beds, paths and lawn edges cleared to the agreed list); a time frame (the day or week of the visit); the work the client must do (move pot plants, keep pets inside, clear the gate); the certainty you provide (a scope checklist and before and after photos, taken with consent); and the risk you carry (the return visit). Put the scope and exclusions in writing. Exclude gutters, roofs, work at height and tree work unless they are separately agreed and within your cover, because this lesson does not cover them. Name the green-waste line on the quote. In Western Australia a quote becomes binding once accepted (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). In Victoria a contract exists whether the agreement was verbal or written (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 9 July 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Simplify booking, access and handover. Record the access route, the bin or green-waste location, and any sprinkler head or irrigation fitting the crew must avoid. Watering matters after a clean-up. In Victoria, a watering system may run only between 6 pm and 10 am (Victorian Government, water.vic.gov.au, updated 13 January 2026). In NSW, Sydney Water limits sprinklers and hoses to before 10 am or after 4 pm (Sydney Water). Say which rule applies to the client's address, and check it before you promise a schedule.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees for services apply and cannot be excluded by contract. Victorian guidance says a tradesperson guarantees due care and skill, fitness for any specified purpose, and completion within a reasonable time where none is set (Consumer Affairs Victoria). A business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge, and the Victorian page does not set a fix-window length (Consumer Victoria, 13 October 2023). A fix-first promise must be one you can keep. A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra on top of these rights (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Do not state a measurable result, such as no regrowth for six months, unless you can show evidence for it.

instruction.heading: Packages that step up in price
instruction.body: Three tiers suit garden work. Good: a one-off garden tidy-up. Better: the tidy-up with a green-waste removal line, priced separately. Best: a monthly upkeep plan with a visit checklist and a photo report. Price each tier from your own cost per productive hour. Market references are vendor ranges: Airtasker lists a garden tidy-up at $120 to $300, a green-waste add-on for a medium garden at $50 to $150, and monthly upkeep at $120 to $220 (Airtasker, updated 18 June 2026). Airtasker is a marketplace and its page gives no method, so treat these as a check only. The Melbourne cost guide lists one trailer or ute load of green waste at $110 to $290, and a landscaper at $50, $72 and $99 per hour (What's the Damage, verified 1 November 2026). Show one total for each tier and say whether GST is included (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026).

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check against cost and time. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). A premium is justified when the client can see the result, has a fixed date and has proof of the work.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a client would repeat, such as 'the beds and paths are clear and photographed on the same day'.
Set a time frame you have checked against your past clean-ups, and record how often you meet it.
List what the client must do, such as moving pot plants and keeping pets inside, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a scope checklist and before and after photos, with consent.
Decide the return-visit guarantee and the green-waste line, and check that you can afford both.
Price from value, then check the rate against cost, time and the vendor ranges.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative: a neglected garden of 80 m², which the owner classes as a medium garden, needs a one-off tidy-up and green-waste removal. The client asks for an hourly rate and says she cannot tell what the job will cost.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which package should the owner offer, and what should the quote show?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner offers a fixed-scope tidy-up with a separate green-waste line. Using the vendor ranges, the tidy-up sits at $120 to $300 and the green-waste add-on at $50 to $150, an illustrative total of $170 to $450 before the owner's own disposal cost. That total is a check, not a price. The owner compares it with the cost guide's $110 to $290 for one trailer or ute load to see whether the add-on is enough, then sets the price from hours and the actual disposal cost. The quote shows each line, says whether GST is included and states the return window. The owner then offers a fortnightly plan at $80 to $160 per visit (Airtasker vendor range), so the one-off job leads to recurring work.

equipmentAndPpe: Scope checklist with before and after photos, taken with consent
Green-waste load record with date and disposal receipt
Quote template with separate lines for tidy-up, green waste and optional extras

commonErrors.error: Pricing a clean-up by the hour with no defined scope
commonErrors.prevention: Quote a fixed scope with a checklist, and price any extra work before starting it.

commonErrors.error: Leaving green-waste removal out of the quote
commonErrors.prevention: Add green-waste removal and disposal as a named line on every clean-up.

commonErrors.error: Promising a result you cannot show
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have measured and can show, such as before and after photos taken with consent.
List gutters, roofs, work at height, tree work and anything outside the agreed list as exclusions.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state rules before acting.

Green-waste carrying and disposal: no Victorian rule was found that applies to a gardener carrying green waste. EPA Victoria's A12 page covers only solid reportable priority waste leaving Victoria and does not mention garden waste (EPA Victoria, 30 May 2025). Council green-waste rules are not confirmed here. Check your council and EPA Victoria before writing the disposal line.

Watering rules are set by state and utility. Victoria: watering systems may run only between 6 pm and 10 am. NSW (Sydney Water): sprinklers and hoses before 10 am or after 4 pm. Check the rule for the state and utility where the garden is.
Pesticide and herbicide use for gardeners in Victoria is not confirmed. This lesson does not offer chemical weed control in any package.

qualityStandard: Every clean-up offer is written, states its exclusions, shows the green-waste line and says whether GST is included.
Each tier price is built from the operator's own costs and checked against the sourced ranges.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with the outcome, time frame, exclusions and return-visit terms
Scope checklist and before and after photo record, with consent
Price worksheet showing cost, margin and the market check
summary: A good garden offer promises a finished result with a date, proof and a fair return visit.
Higher rates follow from clearer value, not from longer hours.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a garden clean-up offer does the customer buy?
What should a return-visit guarantee on a garden clean-up be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford
